clauses.reason: The order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Silk Textile Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act: the operative words of the President's order are "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved, it being distinctly understood that the minimum wage fixed in Article IV applies only to the lowest paid class of labor in the Industry". The approval is stated with the understanding that the Article IV minimum wage applies only to the lowest paid class of labor and that skilled and semi-skilled workers are paid on a higher scale maintaining the July 1, 1933 differentials; that understanding qualifies how the code's wage article applies and operates only through the code. An approved code had legal effect only through section 3 (under 3(b) its provisions became the standards of fair competition, under 3(c) the district courts could enjoin violations, under 3(f) violations were misdemeanors). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The approval therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

research_rationale:
EO 6330 was read in full in the registered APP transcription (common-crawl capture 2025-11-11T06:29:22Z). Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list (1933 Oct 10, p. 542, 'Code of Fair Competition for the Silk Textile Industry approved') and the APP page record with the same sha256 agree on number, date and subject; the page heading names the order's number, its date matches, and the page record's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The order has one operative paragraph: it adopts the Administrator's report and findings and approves the code, with the understanding that the Article IV minimum wage applies only to the lowest paid class and that weavers, warpers, loom fixers and other skilled and semi-skilled workers are to be paid on a higher scale maintaining the dollar differentials of July 1, 1933. Under the shared reviewed analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md, ADJUDICATION.json) a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935, when section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the power to approve or prescribe codes and the provisions enforcing them; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization. Original not yet held; the working text is a labeled transcription under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling.

source_notes.reason: Schechter held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the code provisions there in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization of every section 3 approval (void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end of this order's command; no held record shows that the government cancelled or suspended this code on May 27, 1935.
